title: चतुर्नवत्यधिकद्विशततमोऽध्यायः

summary.en: Karala Janaka says that the sage has taught both oneness and plurality and he finds the point still in doubt. Vasishtha explains how the soul, like wood in the state of nature, neither thinks nor knows, and how creation and dissolution are the unity and the many of nature.
summary.kn: ನಾನಾತ್ವ ಮತ್ತು ಏಕತ್ವ ಎರಡನ್ನೂ ಬೋಧಿಸಿದ್ದೀರಿ, ಇದರಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂಶಯ ಉಳಿದಿದೆ ಎಂದು ಕರಾಲ ಜನಕ ಹೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಪ್ರಕೃತಿ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮರದಂತೆ ಆತ್ಮ ಏನನ್ನೂ ಯೋಚಿಸದು, ತಿಳಿಯದು; ಸೃಷ್ಟಿ-ಪ್ರಳಯಗಳು ಪ್ರಕೃತಿಯ ಏಕತ್ವ ಮತ್ತು ಬಹುತ್ವವೆಂದು ವಸಿಷ್ಠ ವಿವರಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ.
summary.hi: कराल जनक कहते हैं कि ऋषि ने एकत्व और नानात्व दोनों सिखाए और उन्हें इस पर संशय है। वसिष्ठ समझाते हैं कि प्रकृति की अवस्था में आत्मा लकड़ी की तरह न सोचता है न जानता है, और सृष्टि-प्रलय प्रकृति का एकत्व और बहुत्व हैं।
summary.te: నానాత్వం, ఏకత్వం రెండూ బోధించారని, ఇంకా సందేహం ఉందని కరాల జనకుడు అంటాడు. ప్రకృతి స్థితిలో ఆత్మ కొయ్యలా ఏమీ ఆలోచించదు, తెలుసుకోదని, సృష్టి ప్రళయాలు ప్రకృతి ఏకత్వం, బహుత్వమని వసిష్ఠుడు వివరిస్తాడు.
summary.ta: ஒருமையையும் பன்மையையும் போதித்தீர்கள், இதில் இன்னும் ஐயம் உள்ளது என்று கராள ஜனகன் கூற, இயற்கை நிலையில் ஆன்மா மரக்கட்டை போல எதையும் எண்ணாது அறியாது, படைப்பும் அழிவும் இயற்கையின் ஒருமையும் பன்மையும் என்று வசிஷ்டர் விளக்குகிறார்.
summary.ml: ഏകത്വവും ബഹുത്വവും ഉപദേശിച്ചിട്ടും അതിലെ ഒരു ബിന്ദു ഇപ്പോഴും സംശയമായി നിൽക്കുന്നുവെന്ന് കരാള ജനകൻ പറയുന്നു. പ്രകൃതിയിൽ മരം പോലെ ആത്മാവ് ചിന്തിക്കുന്നതോ അറിയുന്നതോ അല്ലെന്നും, സൃഷ്ടിയും ലയവും പ്രകൃതിയുടെ ഏകത്വവും ബഹുത്വവുമാണെന്നും വസിഷ്ഠൻ വിശദീകരിക്കുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 12.294; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Wed Jun 16 2021

verses.text: करालजनक उवाच

meaning.en: Karala Janaka said:

verses.text:
नानात्वैकत्वमित्युक्तं त्वयैतदृषिसत्तम ।
पश्यामि चाभिसंदिग्धमेतयोर्वै निदर्शनम् ॥

meaning.en: You have spoken of manyness and oneness, best of sages, yet I remain doubtful about the example for these two.

verses.text:
तथाप्रबुद्धबुद्धाभ्यां बुध्यमानस्य चानघ ।
स्थूलबुद्ध्या न पश्यामि तत्त्वमेतन्न संशयः ॥

meaning.en: Nor, sinless one, with my coarse understanding do I see the truth of the one who awakens, in relation to the unawakened and the awakened.

verses.text:
अक्षरक्षरयोरुक्तं त्वया यदपि कारणम् ।
तदप्यस्थिरबुद्धित्वात्प्रनष्टमिव मेऽनघ ॥

meaning.en: Even the reason you gave for the imperishable and the perishable has, because my mind is unsteady, seemed to vanish from me.

verses.text:
तदेतच्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि नानात्वैकत्वदर्शनम् ।
बुद्धमप्रतिबुद्धं च बुध्यमानं च तत्त्वतः ॥

meaning.en: So I wish to hear in truth about the view of manyness and oneness, and about the awakened, the unawakened and the awakening one.

verses.text:
विद्याविद्ये च भगवन्नक्षरं क्षरमेव च ।
सांख्यं योगं च कार्त्स्न्येन पृथक्चैवापृथक्च ह ॥

meaning.en: Tell me also, venerable sir, of knowledge and ignorance, the imperishable and the perishable, and of Sankhya and Yoga, in full, both as distinct and as not distinct.

verses.text: वसिष्ठ उवाच

meaning.en: Vasishtha said:

verses.text:
हन्त ते संप्रवक्ष्यामि यदेतदनुपृच्छसि ।
योगकृत्यं महाराज पृथगेव शृणुष्व मे ॥

meaning.en: Very well, I shall explain what you ask. Listen to me, great king, on the practice of Yoga first, by itself.

verses.text:
योगकृत्यं तु योगानां ध्यानमेव परं बलम् ।
तच्चापि द्विविधं ध्यानमाहुर्वेदविदो जनाः ॥

meaning.en: For Yogis the highest strength in the practice of Yoga is meditation; and those who know the Veda say that meditation is of two kinds.

verses.text:
एकाग्रता च मनसः प्राणायामस्तथैव च ।
प्राणायामस्तु सगुणो निर्गुणो मनसस्तथा ॥

meaning.en: They are one-pointedness of mind and control of breath; and the breath control is with qualities, while that of the mind is without qualities.

verses.text:
मूत्रोत्सर्गे पुरीषे च भोजने च नराधिप ।
त्रिकालं नाभियुञ्जीत शेषं युञ्जीत तत्परः ॥

meaning.en: O lord of men, one should not practice at the three times of passing urine, passing stool and eating; at other times one should practice with devotion.

verses.text:
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यो निवर्त्य मनसा मुनिः ।
दशद्वादशभिर्वापि चतुर्विंशात्परं ततः ॥

meaning.en: The sage, turning the senses back from their objects by the mind, whether through ten or twelve, goes beyond the twenty-four.

verses.text:
तं चोदनाभिर्मतिमानात्मानं चोदयेदथ ।
तिष्ठन्तमजरं तं तु यत्तदुक्तं मनीषिभिः ॥

meaning.en: The wise man should then rouse the Self with exhortations, the Self that stands ageless, as the thoughtful have described.

verses.text:
तैश्चात्मा सततं ज्ञेय इत्येवमनुशुश्रुम ।
द्रव्यं ह्यहीनमनसो नान्यथेति विनिश्चयः ॥

meaning.en: We have heard that through those the Self is to be known continually; with an undivided mind one holds the object; it is settled that it is not otherwise.

verses.text:
विमुक्तः सर्वसङ्गेभ्यो लघ्वाहारो जितेन्द्रियः ।
पूर्वरात्रे परे चैव धारयेत मनोऽऽत्मनि ॥

meaning.en: Freed from all attachments, eating lightly, with senses conquered, one should fix the mind in the Self in the first and last parts of the night.

verses.text:
स्थिरीकृत्येन्द्रियग्रामं मनसा मिथिलेश्वर ।
मनो बुद्ध्या स्थिरं कृत्वा पाषाण इव निश्चलः ॥

meaning.en: King of Mithila, having steadied the group of senses by the mind, and made the mind steady by the intellect, one should be motionless like a stone.

verses.text:
स्थाणुवच्चाप्यकम्पः स्याद्गिरिवच्चापि निश्चलः ।
बुधा विधिविधानज्ञास्तदा युक्तं प्रचक्षते ॥

meaning.en: Unshaking like a post and immovable like a mountain: then the wise, who know the rule and method, declare him to be absorbed.

verses.text:
न शृणोति न चाघ्राति न रस्यति न पश्यति ।
न च स्पर्शं विजानाति न संकल्पयते मनः ॥

meaning.en: He does not hear, smell, taste or see; he does not know touch, and the mind forms no intention.

verses.text:
न चाभिमन्यते किंचिन्न च बुध्यति काष्ठवत् ।
तदा प्रकृतिमापन्नं युक्तमाहुर्मनीषिणः ॥

meaning.en: He thinks of nothing as his own and is aware of nothing, like wood; then the wise call him absorbed, having returned to his nature.

verses.text:
निवाते च यथा दीप्यन्दीपस्तद्वत्स दृश्यते ।
निरिङ्गश्चाचलश्चोर्ध्वं न तिर्यग्गतिमाप्नुयात् ॥

meaning.en: He is seen like a lamp burning in a windless place, motionless and unwavering, going neither upward nor sideways.

verses.text:
तदा तमनुपश्येत यस्मिन्दृष्टे तु कथ्यते ।
हृदयस्थोऽन्तरात्मेति ज्ञेयो ज्ञस्तात मद्विधैः ॥

meaning.en: Then one should behold him, on seeing whom he is called the inner Self dwelling in the heart; so one like me should know the knower, dear one.

verses.text:
विधूम इव सप्तार्चिरादित्य इव रश्मिमान् ।
वैद्युतोऽग्निरिवाकाशे दृश्यतेऽऽत्मा तथात्मनि ॥

meaning.en: Like a fire without smoke, like the sun with its rays, like lightning in the sky, the Self is seen in the self.

verses.text:
यं पश्यन्ति महात्मानो धृतिमन्तो मनीषिणः ।
ब्राह्मणा ब्रह्मयोनिष्ठा ह्ययोनिममृतात्मकम् ॥

meaning.en: The great-souled, steadfast sages, the brahmins established in Brahman, see him who is without womb and of the nature of immortality.

verses.text:
तदेवाहुरणुभ्योऽणु तन्महद्भ्यो महत्तरम् ।
तदन्तः सर्वभूतेषु ध्रुवं तिष्ठन्न दृश्यते ॥

meaning.en: They call him subtler than the subtle and greater than the great; he stands firmly within all beings and is not seen.

verses.text:
बुद्धिद्रव्येण दृश्येत मनोदीपेन लोककृत् ।
महतस्तमसस्तात पारे तिष्ठन्नतामसः ॥

meaning.en: The maker of the worlds is seen by the substance of intellect and the lamp of mind; he stands beyond the great darkness, himself free of darkness.

verses.text:
स तमोनुद इत्युक्तस्तत्त्वज्ञैर्वेदपारगैः ।
विमलो वितमस्कश्च निर्लिङ्गोऽलिङ्गसंज्ञितः ॥

meaning.en: Those who know the truth and have crossed the Veda call him the dispeller of darkness: spotless, free of darkness, markless, and called without sign.

verses.text:
योगमेतद्धि योगानां मन्ये योगस्य लक्षणम् ।
एवं पश्यं प्रपश्यन्ति आत्मानमजरं परम् ॥

meaning.en: I consider this the mark of Yoga among the Yogas; those who see thus behold the Self, ageless and supreme.

verses.text:
योगदर्शनमेतावदुक्तं ते तत्त्वतो मया ।
सांख्यज्ञानं प्रवक्ष्यामि परिसंख्यानिदर्शनम् ॥

meaning.en: This much I have told you truly about the vision of Yoga. Now I shall speak of the knowledge of Sankhya, the example based on enumeration.

verses.text:
अव्यक्तमाहुः प्रकृतिं परां प्रकृतिवादिनः ।
तस्मान्महत्समुत्पन्नं द्वितीयं राजसत्तम ॥

meaning.en: Those who teach Nature call the unmanifest the supreme Nature; from it arose the great principle, the second, best of kings.

verses.text:
अहंकारस्तु महतस्तृतीयमिति नः श्रुतम् ।
पञ्च भूतान्यहंकारादाहुः सांख्यानुदर्शिनः ॥

meaning.en: We have heard that egoism is the third after the great principle; and the followers of Sankhya say the five elements come from egoism.

verses.text:
एताः प्रकृतयस्त्वष्टौ विकाराश्चापि षोडश ।
पञ्च चैव विशेषा वै तथा पञ्चेन्द्रियाणि च ॥

meaning.en: These are the eight natures and the sixteen modifications: the five specific elements, and the five senses as well.

verses.text:
एतावदेव तत्त्वानां सांख्यमाहुर्मनीषिणः ।
सांख्ये विधिविधानज्ञा नित्यं सांख्यपथे रताः ॥

meaning.en: The wise call this the full extent of the principles in Sankhya; those expert in its rules always delight in the Sankhya path.

verses.text:
यस्माद्यदभिजायेत तत्तत्रैव प्रलीयते ।
लीयन्ते प्रतिलोमानि सृज्यन्ते चान्तरात्मना ॥

meaning.en: Whatever arises from something is dissolved back into it; things dissolve in reverse order and are again sent forth by the inner Self.

verses.text:
अनुलोमेन जायन्ते लीयन्ते प्रतिलोमतः ।
गुणा गुणेषु सततं सागरस्योर्मयो यथा ॥

meaning.en: They arise in forward order and dissolve in reverse; the qualities ever return into the qualities, like the waves of the ocean.

verses.text:
सर्गप्रलय एतावान्प्रकृतेर्नृपसत्तम ।
एकत्वं प्रलये चास्य बहुत्वं च यदासृजत् ।
एवमेव च राजेन्द्र विज्ञेयं ज्ञेयचिन्तकैः ॥

meaning.en: Such is the extent of Nature's creation and dissolution, best of kings; in dissolution it is one, and when it creates it is many. Those who contemplate the knowable should understand it so, king.

verses.text:
अधिष्ठातारमव्यक्तमस्याप्येतन्निदर्शनम् ।
एकत्वं च बहुत्वं च प्रकृतेरनु तत्त्ववान् ।
एकत्वं प्रलये चास्य बहुत्वं च प्रवर्तनात् ॥

meaning.en: The unmanifest overseer of it also has this illustration. One who knows the principles sees Nature as one and many: one in dissolution, many in the process of emerging.

verses.text:
बहुधात्मा प्रकुर्वीत प्रकृतिं प्रसवात्मिकाम् ।
तच्च क्षेत्रं महानात्मा पञ्चविंशोऽधितिष्ठति ॥

meaning.en: The Self makes Nature, the producer, take many forms; and the great Self, the twenty-fifth, presides over that field.

verses.text:
अधिष्ठातेति राजेन्द्र प्रोच्यते यतिसत्तमैः ।
अधिष्ठानादधिष्ठाता क्षेत्राणामिति नः श्रुतम् ॥

meaning.en: Foremost ascetics, king, call him the overseer; we have heard that from presiding over the fields he is the overseer of fields.

verses.text:
क्षेत्रं जानाति चाव्यक्तं क्षेत्रज्ञ इति चोच्यते ।
अव्यक्तिके पुरे शेते पुरुषश्चेति कथ्यते ॥

meaning.en: He knows the field, the unmanifest, and so is called the knower of the field; he lies in the city of the unmanifest and is called the Person.

verses.text:
अन्यदेव च क्षेत्रं स्यादन्यः क्षेत्रज्ञ उच्यते ।
क्षेत्रमव्यक्तमित्युक्तं ज्ञाता वै पञ्चविंशकः ॥

meaning.en: The field is one thing and the knower of the field is said to be another; the unmanifest is called the field, and the knower is the twenty-fifth.

verses.text:
अन्यदेव च ज्ञानं स्यादन्यज्ज्ञेयं तदुच्यते ।
ज्ञानमव्यक्तमित्युक्तं ज्ञेयो वै पञ्चविंशकः ॥

meaning.en: Knowledge is one thing and the object of knowledge is called another; the unmanifest is called knowledge, and the twenty-fifth is the object to be known.

verses.text:
अव्यक्तं क्षेत्रमित्युक्तं तथा सत्त्वं तथेश्वरम् ।
अनीश्वरमतत्त्वं च तत्त्वं तत्पञ्चविंशकम् ॥

meaning.en: The unmanifest is called the field, as well as goodness and the lord; the twenty-fifth is without lordship and without principle, yet is the principle.

verses.text:
सांख्यदर्शनमेतावत्परिसंख्यानदर्शनम् ।
सांख्यं प्रकुरुते चैव प्रकृतिं च प्रचक्षते ॥

meaning.en: This is the Sankhya view, the view based on enumeration; Sankhya sets forth and describes Nature.

verses.text:
तत्त्वानि च चतुर्विंशत्परिसंख्याय तत्त्वतः ।
सांख्याः सह प्रकृत्या तु निस्तत्त्वः पञ्चविंशकः ॥

meaning.en: The Sankhyas, having counted the twenty-four principles truly, find that the twenty-fifth with Nature stands without principle.

verses.text:
पञ्चविंशोऽप्रबुद्धात्मा बुध्यमान इति स्मृतः ।
यदा तु बुध्यतेऽऽत्मानं तदा भवति केवलः ॥

meaning.en: The twenty-fifth, while unawakened in self, is called the awakening one; when he awakens to the Self, he becomes alone.

verses.text:
सम्यग्दर्शनमेतावद्भाषितं तव तत्त्वतः ।
एवमेतद्विजानन्तः साम्यतां प्रतियान्त्युत ॥

meaning.en: This much correct vision has been told to you truly; knowing it so, people attain equality.

verses.text:
सम्यङ्निदर्शनं नाम प्रत्यक्षं प्रकृतेस्तथा ।
गुणतत्त्वान्यथैतानि निर्गुणोऽन्यस्तथा भवेत् ॥

meaning.en: The right example is direct perception of Nature; these are the principles of the qualities, while the other becomes qualityless.

verses.text:
न त्वेवं वर्तमानानामावृत्तिर्विद्यते पुनः ।
विद्यतेऽक्षरभावत्वादपरस्परमव्ययम् ॥

meaning.en: For those who live thus there is no return again; there is, through the state of imperishability, an undying nature that does not belong to the other.

verses.text:
पश्येरन्नेकमतयो न सम्यक्तेषु दर्शनम् ।
तेऽव्यक्तं प्रतिपद्यन्ते पुनः पुनररिंदम ॥

meaning.en: Those of one view would see; for those with it there is no right vision; they reach the unmanifest again and again, subduer of foes.

verses.text:
सर्वमेतद्विजानन्तो न सर्वस्य प्रबोधनात् ।
व्यक्तीभूता भविष्यन्ति व्यक्तस्य वशवर्तिनः ॥

meaning.en: Knowing all this, but not through awakening to everything, they will become manifest, subject to the manifest.

verses.text:
सर्वमव्यक्तमित्युक्तमसर्वः पञ्चविंशकः ।
य एनमभिजानन्ति न भयं तेषु विद्यते ॥

meaning.en: All is called the unmanifest, while the twenty-fifth is not all; those who know him well have no fear.
